chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy) and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: It was narrated to us by Muhammad ibn Yahya and Ahmad ibn Idris, all of them, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Yahya ibn 'Imran, from al-Sayyari, from Abu Abdillah Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, from al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said:
One who applies perfume at the start of the day while fasting, his intelligence will not decrease.

key_terms.أَوَّلَ النَّهَارِ: at the start of the day

ai.seo_question: Does applying perfume break the fast or affect the intellect of a fasting person according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links the sensory act of applying perfume to the preservation of *'aql* (intellect or mental clarity), suggesting that the pleasant aroma aids in maintaining spiritual focus and preventing the dullness often associated with hunger. This narration is frequently cited by Shia jurists to support the permissibility of using scents during fasting, distinguishing between ingestion and external application, while emphasizing the holistic well-being of the fasting individual.
